newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to issue more zero-coupon bonds.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to issue more zero-coupon bonds.

text.p: Thailand plans to issue another 20 billion baht in zero coupon bonds next week, central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday.
Rerngchai later said the zero-coupon bonds would be issued in tranches of at least five billion baht in weekly auctions over the course of four weeks.
Rerngchai said the zero-coupon bonds issue was part of the government's efforts to raise funds for bailing out the troubled property and financial sectors.

"The central bank has issued a package of measures aimed at creating stability and strengthening these sectors. By the middle of next week there should be new issues of zero coupon bonds of 20 billion baht," Rerngchai told a seminar on future mergers of finance companies.
"We have supported the introduction of various property funds and we will introduce more measures in this direction," he said.
Thailand's first auction of one billion baht of zero-coupon bonds last week was more than four times oversubscribed and produced an average yield of 10.13 percent.

The auction was part of 100 billion baht in zero-coupon bonds planned by the government. In March the government approved the sale of 50 billion baht in zero-coupon bonds but later raised the ceiling to 100 billion baht.
The central bank governor also said the Bank of Thailand was working hard to try and help the property and finance sectors through a variety of measures.
Proceeds from the bonds will be managed by the government-run Property Loans Management Organisation which will purchase non-performing property loans from banks and financial companies.

Analysts estimated that outstanding loans extended to the property sector by commercial banks and finance firms amount to about 800 billion baht, of which 20 to 50 percent could be non-performing. ($1 = 26 baht)
